title: Hooks file and handler discovery
description: Two documents of one boundary. (1) `plugins/batuta/hooks/hooks.json` is the registry and the file Claude Code reads: the event map under a top-level `hooks` key, each entry with the official fields (type, command, args, timeout, if, shell, onFailure, async, statusMessage, once). Every command runs the one launcher `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.py` with the handler id as its last argument: either exec form (`command` a bare interpreter name, `args` the interpreter flags such as -I, the launcher, the id; the rendered default) or shell form (`<interpreter> [flags] "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.py" <id>` with the placeholder in double quotes; the shipped form, with the interpreter `"$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_PYTHON"` and `"shell": "bash"` as decision 19 says); never a machine path. A fail-closed handler (a guard that must block when it cannot decide) sets `onFailure: "block"`, which only the events that can block through it accept (not SessionStart, SubagentStop or Stop: a Stop-type hook returns `decision: block` itself); a fail-open handler (a quality hook) leaves it out. (2) Handler discovery: an area module under `scripts/batuta_lib/areas/` may define a literal `HOOKS = {id: handler}`; the launcher resolves the id across the areas and an id defined twice is a lint failure (`contract lint` reads the modules without importing them and checks that every id of hooks.json resolves to one handler). A handler is `handler(payload: dict) -> dict`: the payload is the C16 input of the event and the returned dict is the handler result (`$defs/handler_result`): `exit_code` 0 or 2, the C16 output object (`output`, or null) and, for exit code 2 (block, shown to the model), the `message`. The launcher prints `output` as JSON on stdout, writes `message` to stderr and exits with `exit_code`; an unknown or missing handler id, an invalid handler result or an exception writes the reason to stderr and exits 1, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking error unless the entry has `onFailure: "block"`. Entry rules: `onFailure` is `continue` (the default) or `block`, and is refused together with `async: true` or `asyncRewake: true` (the platform ignores it there, so a fail-closed entry would fail open); `matcher` is accepted only on PreToolUse, SessionStart and SubagentStop (the platform silently ignores it on Stop and UserPromptSubmit). Two profiles of the same entry check: the shipped profile (`plugins/batuta/hooks/hooks.json`, launcher `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.py`; in shell form the interpreter may be exactly `"$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_PYTHON"` with `"shell": "bash"`) and the rendered profile (`$defs/rendered_entry`: the entries written per device, with an absolute interpreter and an absolute launcher and nothing left to resolve); a document handed to `contract validate` selects the rendered profile with the top-level `"profile": "rendered"`.

profile.description: Only in a document handed to the validator: which entry profile applies (default shipped). The shipped hooks.json Claude Code reads carries none.

matcher.description: What the event is matched against: a tool name or alternatives (Bash, Write|Edit) for PreToolUse, the start source for SessionStart (startup|resume), the agent type for SubagentStop.

command.description: Exec form: a bare interpreter name with args. Shell form: `<interpreter> [flags] "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.py" <handler id>`.

args.description: Exec form: the interpreter flags, then ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook.py, then the handler id.

shell.description: The shell that runs a shell-form command: bash or powershell (the Claude Code settings schema, hooks.*.hooks[].shell).

onFailure.description: continue (the default): a failing hook does not stop the action. block: a hook that fails (non-zero exit other than a decision, a crash, a timeout) blocks the action; fail-closed guards set it. Refused with async or asyncRewake, and block is refused on SessionStart, SubagentStop and Stop.

rendered_entry.description: The rendered profile of an entry: what a device writes into its settings, not what the plugin ships. The same fields and rules as `entry`, except that nothing is left to resolve: the interpreter is a bare name or an absolute path (forward slashes, `/...` or `C:/...`; exec form: the command is the path; shell form: the path in double quotes), the launcher is an absolute path ending in /scripts/hook.py (in double quotes in shell form), and no `{{placeholder}}`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` or `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_PYTHON` remains. Flags, the one handler id, onFailure and matcher rules are those of the shipped profile; `contract.check_hook_entry(entry, event, mode)` checks both.

output.description: A C16 output object (block, pretooluse or sessionstart), or null.

message.description: Required, non-blank, for exit code 2: why the action is blocked.
